subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Regenerative Braking
description: Learn Regenerative Braking in one minute.

hook.text: In an EV, lifting off the accelerator actually slows the car—and charges the battery at the same time.

buildup.text: When you coast, the electric motor runs in reverse, acting as a generator instead of a power source.

discovery.text: The resistance from generating electricity slows the wheels. That electricity goes back into the battery.

twist.text: Some EVs can recover up to 70% of braking energy. Traditional brakes just waste it all as heat.

climax.text: In city driving, regenerative braking can extend range by 20% or more with constant stop-and-go.

punchline.text: EVs brake by turning motion back into power.

quiz.question: How does regenerative braking slow an EV?
options: The motor runs as a generator

details.summary: Regenerative braking captures kinetic energy when slowing down by using the electric motor as a generator, converting motion back into electricity stored in the battery rather than wasting it as heat.
details.whyItMatters: Regen braking can recover 10 to 30 percent of energy that friction brakes would waste as heat, significantly extending EV range especially in stop-and-go city driving.
takeaways: The electric motor reverses role to become a generator when braking
Recovered energy recharges the battery during deceleration
One-pedal driving lets drivers control speed with the accelerator alone

faq.question: Does regenerative braking replace traditional friction brakes?
faq.answer: No. Regen handles light to moderate braking, but hard stops still require friction brakes. Most EVs blend both systems automatically, using regen first and adding friction only when more force is needed.

faq.question: Can regenerative braking fully charge an EV battery?
faq.answer: Not even close. It recovers a fraction of the energy used to accelerate. However, it significantly extends range, especially in urban driving with frequent stops where the cumulative recovery adds up.
